title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages): X is a differentiable manifold and x a point of X. D_x^* is the germ at x of the punctured neighbourhood X∖{x}, viewed as a germ of spaces. The 'sphere of directions' S_x is the space of half-lines in Tang_x(X). A_x is a family of subsets of S_x; to each A in A_x there corresponds a cone C in the tangent space and a germ of spaces Ã over D_x^*. That germ is defined by the filter of sets V∩(C'−{0}), with C' a cone around C, transported by a local diffeomorphism f:(Tang_x X,0)→(X,x). The previous page showed that this filter does not depend on f and that the germs are contractible. This gives the key functor Θ (81) from Π_1(S_x) to coverings of D_x^*. It sends a direction Δ to Θ(Δ) = Revuniv(D_x^*, {Δ}^~), the universal covering fibred at the contractible conical germ around Δ. It is checked to be an equivalence of groupoids, (86 bis), (87), (88).

This page: let γ be a differentiable branch (germ of a C^1 curve) issuing from x, with half-tangent Δ ∈ S_x. Then {Δ} ∈ A_x, and the germ γ minus x lies inside the conical germ {Δ}^~, which lies inside D_x^*. These are the inclusions (91). Both γ and {Δ}^~ are contractible germs, so restricting the fibre of the universal covering gives a canonical isomorphism (92): D^{*~}_{x,γ} := Revuniv(D_x^*, γ) ≅ Revuniv(D_x^*, {Δ}^~) = Θ(Δ).

For a second branch γ' with half-tangent Δ', 'paths' between γ and γ' are defined as Isom(γ,γ') := Isom(D^{*~}_{x,γ}, D^{*~}_{x,γ'}). This is identified, through Θ, with Isom_{Π_1(S_x)}(Δ,Δ'), the homotopy classes of paths on the sphere of directions. That is the bijection (80) being sought.

The next page packages this as a commutative square of equivalences of groupoids (93):
- germs of differentiable branches at x → Π_1(S_x), via γ ↦ Δ(γ);
- Coverings(D_x^*) ≅ Coverings(S_x).

In modern terms, germs of curves at x, through their tangent directions, act as 'tangential base points' for the local fundamental groupoid of the punctured neighbourhood. That groupoid is identified with the fundamental groupoid of the link sphere S^{n-1}. The identification is canonical and does not depend on a chart.
errors: No mathematical error. Implicitly one needs the branch γ minus x to lie eventually inside every conical sector around Δ, which holds because γ is C^1 with nonzero half-tangent. One also needs the conical germs to be contractible, which was argued on the previous page.
Notational slips: in the first displayed line after 'on a donc', the second relation is written '=' rather than '≃'. There is a stray brace in 'Isom(D^{*~}_{x,γ}}, ...)'.

ideas.what: Using germs of differentiable branches (via their half-tangents) as base points for the fundamental groupoid of a punctured neighbourhood, with canonical isomorphism of fibre functors Revuniv(D_x^*,γ) ≅ Θ(Δ)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, 'Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points'); also Ihara, Nakamura in anabelian contexts
ideas.where_published: Possibly alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme / La Longue Marche (base points 'at infinity'); unsure

ideas.what: Equivalence of groupoids between germs of differentiable branches at x and Π_1 of the sphere of directions, and between coverings of the punctured neighbourhood germ and coverings of S_x, defined intrinsically (chart-independent)
ideas.modern_name: local fundamental groupoid at a smooth point ≅ fundamental groupoid of the link; real oriented blow-up
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (real blow-up; Kato–Nakayama-type 'boundary' spaces in log geometry for the algebraic analogue)

missed.claim: Grothendieck develops, in purely differential-topological terms and well before Deligne's 1989 paper, a canonical theory of 'tangential' base points for punctured neighbourhoods. Curve germs are base points, and path classes between them are identified with paths on the sphere of half-tangent directions via a chart-independent functor Θ. This is a documented precursor of tangential base points, not a new result.
missed.quote: Isom(D^{*~}_{x,γ},D^{*~}_{x,γ'}) ≃ Isom(Θ(Δ),Θ(Δ')) ... ≅ Isom_{π_1(S_x)}(Δ,Δ') ce qui est la bijection (80) cherchée.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of historical interest for the genealogy of tangential base points in anabelian geometry and Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory; mathematically elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, chart-free treatment of tangential base points in the differentiable setting, presumably c. 1981, which predates Deligne's published formulation. The mathematics itself is routine and the concept is well known, so this is mainly of historical interest.
